header:
Date: 2027-09-15
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (Venture Medical), Lucas Chen (Venture Medical SRE), Sofia Alvarez (Venture Medical PM)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on model selection and version pinning. Reviewed benchmark results from last week, discussed quantization tradeoffs, rollback/fallback strategies, and next steps for a canary rollout and security documentation.
topics: Model catalog comparison and recommended pin (rdx-13b-q4-pin)
Quantization impacts (8-bit vs 4-bit) and quality regression risk
Fallbacks and rollback plan: region-based, variant-based pinning
Security and compliance questions (KMS, audit logs, data residency)
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick agenda: benchmark review, pinning recommendation, fallback plan, actions.
00:23 Speaker 2 (Maya): Thanks Jordan. we looked at the sample set you sent — the clinical QA set — and initial impressions are pretty good but we saw hallucinations around drug interactions, so want to go slow.
00:45 Speaker 3 (Priya): yeah that's expected when we move to more aggressive quantization. last week we ran the rdx-13b in float32 and 8-bit, and then a 4-bit proto. 8-bit looked within 1.2% quality delta on the 500-case set; 4-bit had a few edge cases.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Lucas): latency numbers? p95 matters for us; we have a 300ms SLO for interactive clinicians.
01:22 Speaker 2 (Priya): right. float32 p95 was ~180ms, 8-bit p95 ~150ms, 4-bit p95 ~120ms on a g5-like instance in our infra. cost per 1k tokens dropped by ~40% at 4-bit vs 8-bit.
01:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): for POC we're recommending pinning to rdx-13b-q4-pin (8-bit quantized) as a balance; fallback to rdx-13b-q0 (float32) if quality regressions detected.
02:10 Speaker 3 (Maya): can you explain the fallback logic? who decides to failover?
02:25 Speaker 2 (Priya): good q. we typically recommend automated rollback triggers: quality regression on a validation prompt set (daily eval), or latency SLO breaches for a sustained period (e.g., 5 minutes at >2x SLO). can also do manual rollback from the console.
02:50 Speaker 4 (Lucas): for us manual is preferred initially; we need an audit trail and approvals. is there RBAC for rollbacks?
03:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yes, RBAC + audit logs in Redwood Private; we can configure who can trigger rollbacks and it logs the change.
03:30 Speaker 5 (Sofia): on the catalog comparison you mentioned earlier — what about smaller models for cost savings? have we compared rdx-7b variants?
03:47 Speaker 2 (Priya): we did a quick comp. rdx-7b is cheaper but accuracy drop on the clinical set was ~6-8% which is outside your stated success criteria. 13b 8-bit gives best hit-rate.
04:10 Speaker 3 (Maya): ok, quality first. Lucas: can we tolerate the cost if rdx-13b is pinned?
04:22 Speaker 4 (Lucas): cost is less of a blocker for pilot but we need to see per-call cost at expected QPS. i'll share traffic profile.
04:40 Speaker 2 (Priya): great — Lucas, if you send the traffic (p50/p95/p99, typical prompt lengths) we'll simulate batching suggestions; Redwood Optimize can recommend batch sizes and caching TTLs.
05:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): last week we also promised a security pack — KMS notes and SOC2 summary. we'll send that after this call.
05:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): on data residency — our infra is in eu-west and we need EU data at rest for PHI; can Redwood Private run in our VPC?
05:35 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yes, Private can be deployed in your VPC or we can provide a region-restricted hosted. for PHI we'd recommend Private with your KMS.
06:00 Speaker 5 (Sofia): any perf gotchas when using your KMS/HSM?
06:12 Speaker 2 (Priya): negligible latency on KMS decrypt on session startup; the main perf is model inference path. Key wraps happen infrequently.
06:30 Speaker 3 (Maya): can we pin to a model and still use Redwood's fallback across regions? we want clinicians in EU to route to EU instances first.
06:50 Speaker 2 (Priya): yes — smart routing supports region-first policies and will fallback to other regions only if capacity constrained. we can pin model version and have per-region pins as well.
07:15 Speaker 4 (Lucas): about rollbacks — is there a way to do canary per percentage of traffic?
07:28 Speaker 2 (Priya): absolutely, canary rollouts by percent and by route. you can do 5/25/100% and have automatic quality checks on the canary.
07:50 Speaker 1 (Jordan): let's review last week's benchmark details — Priya over to you.
08:00 Speaker 2 (Priya): sure — benchmarks were run on 1k synthetic clinical queries + your 500 validation prompts. we measured exact match, F1-ish score proxy, latency p50/p95/p99, and cost. float32 baseline: exact-match 0.82, 8-bit 0.81, 4-bit 0.76. 8-bit had two hallucination types we flagged.
08:35 Speaker 3 (Maya): examples?
08:40 Speaker 2 (Priya): in one, model invented a contraindication for a med; in two others it paraphrased but lost a timeframe. we have those in the shared doc: link to flagged_prompts.xlsx (sent in chat).
09:00 Speaker 5 (Sofia): is there a way to suppress hallucinations by prompt engineering or system messages?
09:12 Speaker 2 (Priya): yes, prompt templates + grounding with retrieval can reduce hallucinations significantly. for the pilot we suggested adding a verification step: model returns sources and a confidence score; downstream rule flags anything below threshold.
09:40 Speaker 4 (Lucas): technically we'll need the model to expose token-level latency so we can trace long tails; can Redwood provide traces?
09:53 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yes, Redwood Console provides per-request traces, token timing, and KV cache hit rates.
10:10 Speaker 3 (Maya): on the pin recommendation, will pinning to rdx-13b-q4-pin lock us from applying security patches or improvements?
10:25 Speaker 2 (Priya): pinning fixes the model binary version; safety patches and infra updates still roll through. if you want automatic model improvements we can do controlled rollouts to newer model revisions.
10:45 Speaker 5 (Sofia): what's the naming convention for pinned models?
10:50 Speaker 2 (Priya): we use rdx-<size>-<tag>-pin when pinned, e.g., rdx-13b-q4-pin, and keep history of previous revisions.
11:10 Speaker 1 (Jordan): let's talk about detection for quality regressions — how frequent are your evals?
11:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): daily scheduled evals on the validation set; threshold breaches trigger alerts and can auto-remove a pin if desired — but we'll keep that off until you're comfortable.
11:45 Speaker 4 (Lucas): how do we validate that rollback happened and it didn't cause a spike in latency? need correlation dashboards.
11:58 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Console includes model rollout dashboards with latency and error rate by variant; we'll set up alerting to notify SRE channel.
12:15 Speaker 3 (Maya): curious about mixed-precision — will 8-bit and 4-bit mix cause cache incompatibilities?
12:30 Speaker 2 (Priya): KV cache keys are variant-aware; mixing variants invalidates some caches, so you can get cold-cache spikes on rollback. we recommend staged canaries and cache-warm strategies.
13:00 Speaker 5 (Sofia): ok noted. next, pricing — if we pin 13b 8-bit for pilot volume (approx 100k tokens/day), what's ballpark?
13:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we'll send an updated per-token estimate but ballpark for 13b 8-bit is $X per 1k tokens; 4-bit reduces cost further. detailed pricing in the sheet I'll share.
13:35 Speaker 4 (Lucas): please include burst capacity pricing — we might have spike events.
13:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): will do.
14:00 Speaker 2 (Priya): any other open technical blockers?
14:05 Speaker 3 (Maya): can you run a focused regression test around drug interaction prompts after quantization? that's priority.
14:18 Speaker 2 (Priya): yes, we'll prioritize that in the benchmark runs. Priya: action for the drug-interaction regression.
14:30 Speaker 5 (Sofia): timeline for next steps?
14:35 Speaker 1 (Jordan): recap: Priya runs the 1k benchmark incl chase of the flagged prompts by 9/22; Jordan sends security and pricing by 9/17; Lucas sends traffic profile by 9/20; Sofia confirms quality thresholds by 9/21. we'll meet next Wednesday same time.
14:58 Speaker 4 (Lucas): small ask — can we get a sample of the canary rollout UI?
15:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): yes, we'll record a 10-min demo clip and share link.
15:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
15:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): thanks team — end of call.
45:00 [meeting ended]
